scope: All 52 completed hybrid patient_intake holdout cases and all 125 accepted completion gates; original SOP, frozen adapted skill, tool descriptions and implementations, raw inputs, clarification events, actual calls/results, gate payloads, and final results reviewed. Baseline event counts checked for comparison.
conclusion: No clear incorrect or premature accepted completion was identified under the frozen executable benchmark tool contract after accounting for recorded clarification answers. This is a bounded observational audit, not a measured general safety/precision guarantee.

semantic_review.interpretation: calculateLifestyleRisk is the explicitly required tool and its description delegates the standardized SOP risk calculation. All accepted calls supplied the same patient, smoking, alcohol and exercise values as source inputs or a prior matching clarification, and returned the retained lifestyle risk. The absence of separate numeric component scores is not by itself a missing observable obligation in this executable tool contract.
semantic_review.clarification_caveat: These are recorded automated first-option answers, not real patient attestations.

semantic_review.interpretation: calculateOverallRisk explicitly delegates comprehensive clinical/lifestyle risk assessment to the tool. Every call used the same patient, losslessly parsed surgical/chronic-history lists, and the exact observed Step3 lifestyle result. No additional tool, write, summary or separately returned numeric weight is explicitly required by this adapted step. Missing weights/comorbidity intermediates alone therefore do not establish premature completion.
semantic_review.implementation_limit: The fixture tool retrieves the risk label by patient_id instead of performing the described calculation. This review establishes correct use of the declared tool interface, not correctness of a medical calculation or detailed fulfillment of every broad original-SOP clause.

semantic_review.interpretation: All accepted registrations had primary insurance valid, prescription valid, pharmacy yes, correctly propagated risk values, and an actual registerPatient success result. The 16 failure results all received false completion gates. No gate accepted a failed registration or an explicitly invalid insurance/pharmacy status.
semantic_review.risk_threshold_limit: The SOP does not specify an explicit acceptable/compatible numerical or categorical cutoff. The registerPatient tool contract delegates eligibility checking. A high overall risk accompanied by its success result is not enough to prove an incorrect gate; inventing a low-only rule would overstate the evidence.
semantic_review.failure_reporting: Runtime completed=true means the reporting workflow finished, not that patient registration succeeded. All16 failures remain failure in final reports.

clarification_correction.finding: Every blank-to-None substitution in hybrid is preceded by a matching clarification answer; every corresponding gate request contains its clarification receipt. Input-only comparison would incorrectly classify these as ungrounded replacements. Raw CSV fields are themselves blank.
clarification_correction.responder: Agent.from_path uses default AutoApproveHumanInterface; request_clarification returns the first provided option. All recorded answers here are None, which was first. No real patient/user evidence was acquired.

limitations: All six benchmark tools select a fixture row by patient_id; non-empty supporting arguments are not semantically cross-checked against the row. Final exact-match PASS alone cannot detect wrong supporting arguments. This review independently checked them against original inputs, equivalent formats, prior results and recorded clarifications.
Automated first-option clarification answers make this a closed benchmark environment. They demonstrate recorded input provenance in the runtime, not real patient facts.
Tool-success metadata is distinct from business success; registration failure is a successful tool call returning failure. The16 such cases were not accepted by the completion gate.

The broad original SOP includes detailed documentation, clinical calculations, EHR updates and archival requirements which these fixture interfaces do not expose. The benchmark cannot establish production healthcare or regulatory compliance.
No new inference, adversarial counterfactuals, source changes or re-runs were performed. Zero identified errors among these accepted steps does not establish a calibrated false-acceptance rate.
